approachQuestion.prompt: A meter starts at value 0 with no active edits. An immutable list contains n commands, 0 <= n <= 200,000. CHANGE(d) adds signed integer d and records an active edit, even when d is zero. UNDO reverses the most recent still-active CHANGE and removes that edit; with no active edits it does nothing. READ appends the current value to the returned list. There is no redo. All values and arithmetic results fit signed 64-bit integers. Return the READ values in command order. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total processing time. Input: [CHANGE(6), CHANGE(-2), UNDO, READ, CHANGE(3), UNDO, UNDO, READ]. Output: [6,0].

options.text: Keep the current value and a stack of active deltas. CHANGE adds and pushes d. UNDO pops and subtracts the delta if present. READ appends the current value.
options.feedback: The latest active delta is exactly the change to reverse; its sign must be preserved.

options.text: Keep the current value and a stack of prior values. Before CHANGE push the current value, then add d. UNDO restores and pops the top if present; READ records the current value.
options.feedback: A prior value restores precisely the state before the latest active change, using the same amount of work and storage as deltas.

options.text: Store active deltas in a queue; UNDO subtracts and removes the oldest delta.
options.feedback: For [CHANGE(6),CHANGE(-2),UNDO,READ], this reports -2 instead of 6 because undo must reverse the newest edit.

options.text: Push the absolute value of every delta and subtract the top on UNDO.
options.feedback: For [CHANGE(-2),UNDO,READ], this reports -4 rather than 0. Undoing a negative delta requires adding its magnitude.

feedback.reason: Undo reverses the most recent active change; either inverse deltas or prior scalar values preserve enough information.
details: Store each CHANGE delta while adding it to the current value. For a nonempty UNDO, pop the newest delta and subtract it. Empty UNDO does nothing; READ appends the current value.
Undo removes the latest active delta, not the last READ or a previously undone change. Subtracting that saved delta reverses its contribution; empty UNDO leaves the value unchanged.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For undo-delta-stack, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The input is immutable and excluded from auxiliary space. Returned output is excluded, but all working buffers count even if later copied into output.
Fixed-size integers, characters, indices and comparisons take constant time. Arithmetic is unit cost under the stated range guarantee.
Use an iterative implementation with a preallocated n-entry array and a top index: push and pop take constant time. No recursion, hashing, or hidden whole-buffer copies occur.
Materializing output takes time proportional to its length; no persistent snapshots or string concatenation are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Process commands once and retain the active change history.
details: Each command performs bounded work and each READ writes one result. All n commands may be CHANGE, leaving n active deltas even with an empty result. Thus total time and auxiliary stack space are O(n). No document snapshots or recursion are involved.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: n consecutive CHANGE commands retain n undoable deltas even if no READ output is produced.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each CHANGE pushes one delta and each successful UNDO removes one; command prefixes are not replayed to recover old values.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final CHANGE or UNDO can affect a later READ, so arbitrary command streams require a full worst-case scan.
